ru: ослабевать, ослабеть; стихать, стихнуть
separable: intransitive — it takes no object at all: *the rain eased up*, never *ease up the rain*
gloss: To become less strong, less severe, or less fast.
examples: The rain should *ease up* by noon.
Traffic finally *eased up* after the exit.
The pressure at work hasn't *eased up* since March.

ru: ослаблять нажим, ослабить нажим; убавлять, убавить
separable: inseparable — the object always follows *on*: *ease up on him*, never *ease him up on*
transitivity: transitive — always with *on* before the object
gloss: To treat someone less harshly, or to use less of something.
examples: *Ease up on* the kid — he's only eight.
The coach *eased up on* us after the first week.
I've been *easing up on* coffee since the checkup.

ru: ослабевать, ослабеть; убавлять, убавить
separable: intransitive — no object; to name what you are cutting back on, add *on*: *ease off on the salt*
gloss: To become less intense, or to do something with less force than before.
examples: Rain like this usually *eases off* by morning.
The wind *eased off* around midnight.
He's *easing off* on the overtime this month.

ru: постепенно втягиваться, втянуться; входить в курс, войти в курс
separable: inseparable — the object follows *into*: *ease into the job*, never *ease the job into*; only a reflexive comes first: *ease yourself into it*
gloss: To start something slowly and gently instead of all at once.
examples: Give yourself a week to *ease into* the new schedule.
She *eased into* the job with almost no training.
He's *easing into* running again after the injury.

ru: вытеснять, вытеснить; выживать, выжить (с должности)
separable: separable — *ease him out*, and *ease out the old manager*; where he leaves from takes *of*: *eased out of the company*
gloss: To remove someone from a job or position quietly, without an open firing.
examples: The board wants to *ease* him *out* before the merger.
The founder was quietly *eased out* last spring.
They're *easing out* the whole senior team, one at a time.

ru: обыгрывать с минимальным перевесом, обыграть; опережать, опередить
separable: separable — *edge them out*, and *edge out the defending champions*
gloss: To beat someone by a very small margin.
examples: Miami *edged out* Boston by a single point.
She has *edged out* the favorite twice this season.
He's *edging* her *out* by two points with one round left.

ru: вытеснять, вытеснить; оттеснять, оттеснить
separable: separable — *edge her out*, and *edge out the older staff*; very often passive: *he was edged out*
gloss: To push someone slowly out of a job, a market, or a position.
examples: Cheap imports *edge out* the local makers every time.
He was *edged out* by a younger partner.
The big chains are *edging* small grocers *out* of the neighborhood.

ru: понемногу расти, вырасти; медленно повышаться, повыситься
separable: intransitive — no object: *prices edged up*, never *edge up the prices*
gloss: Of a number or a price, to rise slowly by a small amount.
examples: Gas prices *edge up* every summer.
Unemployment *edged up* to four percent.
Rents have been *edging up* all year.

ru: подначивать, подначить; подбивать, подбить; подстрекать
separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *egg him on*, never *egg on him*; a full noun can go either way: *egg the crowd on* / *egg on the crowd*
gloss: To urge someone on to do something reckless or foolish.
examples: Don't *egg* him *on* — he'll actually jump.
His friends *egged* him *on* until he ate the whole thing.
The crowd was *egging* them *on* from the sidewalk.
contrast: Nothing to do with breakfast: this *egg* is an old Norse word meaning *to urge*. The forms are *egged on*, *egging on* — the *gg* is already there, so nothing doubles.

ru: растягивать, растянуть (запасы); с трудом добывать, добыть; перебиваться
separable: separable — *eke out a living*, and *eke it out*; with a full noun the object almost always follows the whole phrase
gloss: To manage to live on very little, or to make a small supply last.
examples: They *eke out* a living on forty acres.
He *eked out* his savings for another year.
She's been *eking out* the last of the firewood.
contrast: *Eke* rhymes with *week*, not with *wreck*: /iːk/, EEK. The silent *-e* drops in *eking out*.

ru: с трудом добиваться, добиться; вырывать, вырвать (победу)
separable: separable — *eke out a win*, and *eke it out*
gloss: To win or achieve something by the smallest of margins.
examples: A good quarter lets them *eke out* a profit.
The Cavaliers *eked out* a two-point win in overtime.
She's *eking out* a lead of just three hundred votes.

ru: опорожнять, опорожнить; вытряхивать, вытряхнуть; освобождать, освободить
separable: separable — *empty it out*, and *empty out the closet*
gloss: To take everything out of a container, a room, or a pocket.
examples: *Empty out* your pockets before you wash those jeans.
We *emptied out* the whole garage on Saturday.
She's *emptying out* her desk — today is her last day.
contrast: The *-y* turns to *-ie*: *empties out*, *emptied out*, but the *-ing* form keeps it — *emptying out*.

ru: пустеть, опустеть; пустовать
separable: intransitive — no object in this sense: *the stadium emptied out*
gloss: Of a place, to become empty as the people in it leave.
examples: The beach *empties out* right after Labor Day.
The theater *emptied out* in five minutes.
The office is *emptying out* early today.

ru: оказываться, оказаться; в итоге попадать, попасть
separable: intransitive — no object; a place, an adjective, or an *-ing* form follows: *ended up in Denver*, *ended up broke*, *ended up paying twice*
gloss: To finally be in a place or a situation you did not plan on.
examples: Keep skipping class and you'll *end up* repeating the year.
We *ended up* in Denver because of the storm.
She has *ended up* doing most of the work herself.
contrast: What follows *end up* is an *-ing* form, never an infinitive: *ended up paying twice*, not *ended up to pay twice*.

ru: оставаться, остаться с (чем-л.); получать, получить в итоге
separable: inseparable — the object always follows *with*: *end up with the bill*, never *end the bill up with*
gloss: To have something at the end of it all, usually not what you intended.
examples: Order carefully or you'll *end up with* two of everything.
I *ended up with* the bill again.
They've *ended up with* a house they can't afford.

ru: заканчиваться, закончиться (чем-л.); приводить, привести (к чему-л.)
separable: inseparable — the result follows *in*: *ended in a tie*, never *ended a tie in*
gloss: To have a particular result or outcome.
examples: Arguments like that usually *end in* nothing.
The game *ended in* a tie.
Their marriage has *ended in* divorce.

ru: вступать, вступить (в договор, переговоры); заключать, заключить
separable: inseparable — the object follows *into*: *enter into a contract*, never *enter a contract into*
gloss: To formally begin an agreement, a contract, or a set of talks.
examples: Both sides *enter into* the contract freely.
The city *entered into* an agreement with the developer.
They have *entered into* negotiations with the union.

ru: приниматься в расчёт, играть роль; иметь отношение (к делу)
separable: inseparable — and in this sense almost always with *it*: *money doesn't enter into it*
gloss: To be a factor in something, or to be part of what matters.
examples: Money doesn't *enter into* it — I just don't want to go.
Her age never *entered into* the decision.
Politics has *entered into* every part of the debate.

ru: выравниваться, выровняться; выравнивать, выровнять
separable: separable when it takes an object — *even it out*, and *even out the workload*; just as often it takes none: *things will even out*
transitivity: both — transitive (even out the workload), intransitive (the numbers even out)
gloss: To become level or equal over time, or to make something level or equal.
examples: Costs *even out* over the year.
We *evened out* the workload after the complaints.
Prices are *evening out* now that the shortage is over.
contrast: *Evening out* is spelled like the noun *evening*, but the verb keeps three syllables — EE-vuhn-ing, not EEV-ning.

ru: уравнивать, уравнять; сравнивать, сравнять (счёт)
separable: separable — *even up the score*, and *even it up*
gloss: To make two things equal, especially a score or a share.
examples: That penalty *evens up* the score.
He paid for dinner to *even* things *up*.
One more basket would have *evened* it *up*.

ru: оправдывать, оправдать (объяснениями); отговариваться, отговориться
separable: separable — *explain it away*, and *explain away the missing money*; with a pronoun it must split: *explain them away*
gloss: To make something bad look unimportant by giving reasons or excuses for it.
examples: He can *explain away* almost anything.
She *explained away* the missing hours as a clerical error.
You can't keep *explaining* these numbers *away*.

ru: подробнее рассказывать, рассказать; развивать, развить (мысль)
separable: inseparable — the object follows *on*: *expand on the idea*, never *expand the idea on*
gloss: To say or write more about something you have already mentioned.
examples: Could you *expand on* that last point?
She *expanded on* the idea in her second book.
He's *expanding on* the proposal in tomorrow's memo.
contrast: *Expand on* and *elaborate on* mean the same thing. *Expand* on its own only means to get bigger: *the company expanded*.

ru: приступать, приступить (к чему-л.); начинать, начать; пускаться, пуститься
separable: inseparable — the object follows *on*: *embark on a career*, never *embark a career on*; *embark upon* is the formal variant
gloss: To start something big or long, such as a project, a journey, or a career.
examples: Next month they *embark on* a three-year study.
She *embarked on* a second career at fifty.
The country has *embarked on* the largest rebuild in its history.
